papers.title: Microglia stabilize sleep homeostasis via adenosine A3 receptor signaling.
papers.summary: Using miniaturized two-photon microscopy in freely behaving mice, the study shows that microglial calcium activity is rapidly altered by brain-state transitions and is predominantly mediated by adenosine A3 receptor (A3R) signaling in response to state-dependent extracellular adenosine oscillations. Microglia-specific A3R deletion attenuated state-dependent calcium dynamics, impaired morphological plasticity across sleep-wake cycles, and increased wake-NREM transitions, indicating that microglia stabilize sleep homeostasis through eADO-A3R signaling.

papers.title: Acoustic enhancement of slow wave sleep improves memory retention by coordinating brain oscillatory rhythms and autonomic activity.
papers.summary: In a randomized, single-blind, crossover study of 20 healthy young adults, one night of closed-loop acoustic stimulation of slow waves during NREM sleep enhanced memory retention on a paired word-associates task compared to sham. Memory enhancement was associated with an increased SO/δ-spindle nesting ratio and elevated parasympathetic activity (heart rate variability) during SWS, which were strongly correlated and predicted memory performance.

papers.title: Differential associations of arousals and respiratory events on oxygen desaturation and resaturation parameters in sleep.
papers.summary: In 5,484 Sleep Heart Health Study participants, pre-event arousals (≤10 s before desaturation onset) were associated with faster desaturation rates and shorter desaturation durations, while within-event arousals were associated with lower nadirs, longer desaturations, and larger desaturation areas; both arousal types increased resaturation rates via distinct mechanisms (pre-event shortened resaturation duration, within-event increased resaturation height), with effects amplified during apnoeas.

papers.title: Sleep whistling and replaying a melody during N3 sleep: a new form of disorder of arousal.
papers.summary: In a 30-year-old man with a history of childhood sleepwalking and confusional arousals, video-polysomnography captured a whistled melody ('Take Me Home, Country Roads') with coordinated rhythmic upper-body movements during a spontaneous slow-wave arousal from N3 sleep; he had complete amnesia but later recognized the melody, expanding the behavioral repertoire of arousal disorders.

papers.title: Natural sleep, but not propofol-induced anesthesia preserves spatial and procedural memory consolidation
papers.summary: Comparing 19 participants undergoing propofol-induced anesthesia with 17 participants taking a nap, performance on hippocampus-dependent spatial and procedural memory tasks declined from pre to post in the propofol group but remained stable in the sleep group. Although slow oscillations occurred in both conditions, only during non-REM sleep did SOs show increased spindle activity during the SO upstate, suggesting that propofol anesthesia disrupts memory consolidation because SOs lack spindle coupling.

papers.title: A unified signal-quality assessment framework for synchronized electro-intravascular encephalography and scalp electroencephalography.
papers.summary: Proposed a unified signal-quality assessment framework for electro-intravascular encephalography (EiEG) and validated it in an ovine model with a stent-mounted electrode in the superior sagittal sinus. EiEG showed high physiological concordance with scalp EEG (Spearman's ρ>0.94), higher spectral fidelity (linear SNR ratios 2.04 vs Cz, 1.84 vs C1), and greater across-bout consistency (CV 0.8% vs 29.8%), with no acute complications.

papers.title: Clinical utility of in-ear EEG electrodes in hospitalized patients: comparison with standard scalp EEG.
papers.summary: In 30 hospitalized adults, in-ear EEG compared with standard scalp EEG showed 83.3% sensitivity, 80.0% specificity, and 82.8% accuracy for detecting any neurophysiological abnormality, with substantial agreement for encephalopathy grading (weighted kappa 0.72); one focal seizure was missed by ear EEG, suggesting utility for diffuse dysfunction but limited spatial coverage.

papers.title: Changes in sleep characteristics in Parkinson's disease: a prospective 5-year follow-up study.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
papers.summary: In a 5-year prospective cohort of 183 Parkinson's disease patients, daytime sleepiness, napping, sleep talking, nightmares, RBD-related symptoms, and restless legs syndrome increased significantly, while insomnia symptoms, circadian timing, and total sleep time remained stable; excessive daytime sleepiness was independently associated with depressive symptoms, dopamine agonist use, and sleep apnea risk.

papers.title: Sustained hypoxia induces divergent response patterns in cardiac metabolic-immune adaptation and circadian rhythm regulation.
papers.summary: Comparative transcriptomic analysis of three hypoxia paradigms using GEO datasets found that sustained hypoxia induced 181 DEGs, prenatal hypoxia produced only 2, and adult subacute hypoxia yielded 67, with no overlap among groups. The circadian interactome showed dramatic remodeling with gene pairs decreasing by 67.5%, ASS1 emerged as the predominant co-expression hub under hypoxia, and pathway analysis revealed divergent enrichment profiles between metabolic-immune and circadian systems.

papers.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization.
papers.journal: Digest of technical papers. Symposium on VLSI Technology
papers.summary: This work presents a 65 nm SoC for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation that performs low-noise EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A memory reuse technique and runtime dynamic quantization reduced model size by 3.88× with only 0.28% accuracy loss, achieving 98.3% sensitivity for deep sleep detection.

papers.title: Modeling the Exposome in Murine Cardiovascular Disease.
papers.summary: Reviews experimental approaches for modeling environmental and lifestyle exposures (sleep, stress, exercise, smoking, viral respiratory infections, pollution) in murine cardiovascular disease models. Highlights emerging evidence for causal holistic mechanisms linking the exposome to cardiovascular pathophysiology.

papers.title: MRI-informed multi-modal deep learning for EEG source imaging with subject-specific head structure recognition.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors developed a subject-specific multi-modal deep learning framework integrating EEG and MRI-derived head models for EEG source imaging, achieving 5 mm localization error and 1.64 ms inference time in simulation, outperforming conventional inverse methods and uni-modal baselines, with robustness across diverse head anatomies and preserved advantage on intracranial-stimulation data.

papers.title: Heartfulness Meditation-induced State and Trait Effects on Long-term, Short-term and Non-meditators Using Connectivity Analysis: An EEG Study on Prefrontal Cortex.
papers.summary: EEG study recorded prefrontal activity in long-term, short-term, and non-meditators across baseline, meditation, transmission, and post-transmission states to assess Heartfulness meditation state and trait effects. Functional connectivity and graph theory measures showed increased global and local efficiency during meditation, with significant trait-level changes in delta, theta, and alpha bands in long-term meditators.

papers.title: Polygenic score for sleep duration in relation to the risk of Alzheimer's disease: results from the UK biobank.
papers.summary: Using wearable-derived sleep duration GWAS in 77,770 UK Biobank participants, the authors generated polygenic scores and tested their association with Alzheimer's disease in 264,746 independent participants (1,451 cases). The highest fifth of genetically predicted sleep duration (about 15 min/day longer sleep) had lower Alzheimer's disease risk (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.67-0.94).

papers.title: Modifiable Physiological Factors Associated With Human Glymphatic and Interstitial Fluid Dynamics-Related Measures: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped human evidence on non-pharmacological modifiable physiological factors associated with glymphatic and interstitial fluid dynamics-related measures, including 105 studies from 4134 records. Sleep quality/architecture/insomnia (n=45) and blood pressure/hypertension (n=25) were the largest domains, but evidence was dominated by observational studies and surrogate outcomes.

papers.title: Sleep Variability From Routine Nursing Observation and Wearable Actigraphy for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients: Prospective Observational Study
papers.summary: Prospective observational study assessed whether early sleep instability during the first 7 days of hospitalization predicts prolonged length of stay in 94 acute psychiatric inpatients using wrist actigraphy and routine nursing observation. Greater actigraphy-derived sleep variability was associated with prolonged hospitalization (OR 2.42 per 1-hour increase; AUC 0.75), and nursing-derived sleep variability also carried independent prognostic information (adjusted OR 3.02; AUC 0.70).

papers.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: The paper studies subject-level differential privacy for clinical EEG-derived feature representations using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations across client-side, server-side, and decentralized training scenarios. Results show that perturbation can be integrated into EEG workflows, but mechanism choice, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly affect data utility, highlighting a privacy-utility trade-off in small and imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm Disruption in Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanistic Insights, Diagnostic Implications, and Emerging Chronotherapeutic Strategies: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the role of circadian rhythm disruption in Alzheimer's disease, detailing how decreased melatonin secretion, sleep disturbances, altered suprachiasmatic nucleus signaling, clock gene mutations, and glymphatic clearance impairment link to amyloid-β buildup, tau pathology, neuroinflammation, and cognitive decline. It highlights chronotherapies such as melatonin supplementation, light therapy, and sleep hygiene as promising strategies for restoring circadian regulation and enhancing cognitive performance.

papers.title: The hypoxic burden algorithm: an integrated index for assessing intermittent hypoxia in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea-a retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort of 115 children with suspected obstructive sleep apnea compared a new hypoxic burden algorithm against conventional nocturnal hypoxic metrics from polysomnography. Hypoxic burden showed the strongest correlation with obstructive apnea-hypopnea index (r=0.801) and the best diagnostic performance (AUC 0.888) among the assessed indices.

papers.title: No Influence of Sleep Quality and Chronotype on the Effects of Mental Fatigue: Evidence From an Exploratory Analysis.
papers.summary: This exploratory analysis tested whether sleep quality and chronotype moderate subjective, cognitive, and physical responses to a 45-minute Stroop-induced mental fatigue task versus a control documentary. Most outcomes showed no meaningful moderation, though sleep quality (p=0.028) and chronotype (p=0.002) influenced general subjective mental fatigue, and chronotype groups differed in sleepiness (p<0.001).

papers.title: Machine learning identifies depression risk in older adults with chronic diseases: Clarifying shared risk factors stratified by cognitive impairment status.
papers.summary: Developed machine learning models (XGBoost with SHAP) using data from 5,798 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey participants to identify depression risk in older adults with chronic diseases, stratified by cognitive impairment status. Models achieved accuracies of 0.755–0.767 and Brier scores ≤0.160; top predictors differed by cognitive status ('feeling energetic' for cognitively unimpaired/mildly impaired, 'sleep duration per day' for severely impaired).

papers.title: Hypoxic Burden from Obstructive Sleep Apnoea is Increased in Pacific Islanders with distinct Pathophysiological Traits.
papers.summary: In a retrospective comparison of 42 Pacific Islanders and 62 Caucasians with obstructive sleep apnoea, Pacific Islanders had similar apnoea-hypopnoea index but significantly higher mean apnoea length, oxygen desaturation index, average desaturation, time with SpO2 <90%, and hypoxic burden (adjusted mean difference 67.4 %·min/h, p=0.012). They also exhibited distinct endotypes including higher REM arousal threshold, lower REM Vpassive, and higher NREM loop gain, suggesting that OSA in this population is characterized by longer apnoeas and increased hypoxic burden.

papers.title: The protective role of resilience-related strength in the association between sleep reactivity and insomnia symptoms among young Chinese male university students: a moderated network approach.
papers.summary: Among 1,122 young Chinese male university students, sleep reactivity was positively associated with insomnia symptoms, and the resilience dimension Strength negatively associated with and moderated this relationship, with moderated network analysis localizing the moderation to specific sleep reactivity-insomnia links involving interpersonal conflict and public speaking.

papers.title: Reduced Motor Preparation and Altered EEG Signatures of Prediction in Autistic Adults.
papers.summary: In a preregistered EEG experiment, autistic adults showed less behavioral benefit from high-probability auditory cues and a reduced late CNV motor preparatory potential compared with IQ- and language-matched non-autistic controls, alongside shallower 1 Hz ramping potentials and reduced posterior phase entrainment.

papers.title: Pluripotency and Transcriptional Pausing Disrupt Circadian Rhythms to Facilitate the Enrichment of Cancer Stem Cells
papers.summary: Carboplatin-treated triple-negative breast cancer cells lost circadian rhythms and enriched cancer stem cells, and genetic circadian clock ablation alone promoted cancer stem cell formation and tumorsphere/tumor generation; OCT4 disrupted circadian gene expression, and restoring rhythms in Oct4-deficient cells impaired tumorsphere formation and reduced cancer stem cells in mouse tumors.

papers.title: Effect of active noise-cancelling headphones combined with music therapy on postoperative recovery quality after general anaesthesia for ankle fracture ORIF: a study protocol for a single-centre, four-arm 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial in China.
papers.summary: This is a protocol for a single-centre, four-arm 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial in China that will enrol 224 adults undergoing ankle fracture ORIF to test active noise-cancelling headphones combined with music therapy on postoperative recovery quality. The primary outcome is the QoR-15 score at 24 hours postoperatively, with secondary outcomes including pain, anxiety, sleep quality, melody recognition, opioid consumption, and adverse events.

papers.title: Behavioral Sleep Treatment in ADHD Across Child and Adolescent Development: Recent Findings, Integration with Existing Interventions, and Emerging Directions.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in behavioral sleep interventions for youth with ADHD across early childhood, middle childhood, and adolescence, emphasizing developmental considerations. It reports growing evidence supporting the feasibility and effectiveness of such interventions, particularly for improving parent- and self-reported sleep outcomes, and identifies emerging directions for integrating sleep-focused strategies into existing ADHD treatments.

papers.title: Vascular and neurodegenerative contributions to cognitive decline and multidomain progression in de novo Parkinsons disease
papers.summary: Longitudinal study of de novo Parkinson's disease patients from PPMI examined vascular and neurodegenerative contributions to cognitive decline and multidomain progression. Among 350 participants, 58 converters showed faster cognitive, motor, gait, neuropsychiatric, sleep, and functional decline, with higher baseline white matter hyperintensity burden but no accelerated accumulation, alongside accelerated limbic and subcortical atrophy.

papers.title: Role of the circadian rhythm in squamous cell carcinoma: From molecular mechanism to therapy (Review).
papers.summary: This review summarizes current knowledge on circadian regulation in squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), focusing on core clock genes, their interactions with oncogenic and immune pathways, and therapeutic implications including chronotherapy. It highlights limitations such as predominance of preclinical studies and limited SCC-specific clinical evidence, and outlines key research priorities.

papers.title: Clinical risk stratification of stroke caregiver distress: an interpretable nonlinear model of caregiving-load categories.
papers.summary: This multicenter cross-sectional study developed an interpretable XGBoost model using six predictor domains to stratify high psychological distress among 506 stroke caregivers. The model achieved a test-set AUC of 0.890, with role burnout, active coping, and perceived social support as top predictors, and interaction plots suggesting load-dependent associations.

papers.title: Validation of the Korean version of the Sleep, Circadian Rhythms, And Mood (SCRAM) questionnaire.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated the Korean version of the Sleep, Circadian Rhythms, and Mood (SCRAM) questionnaire in 528 respondents. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a three-factor structure (Good Sleep, Morningness, Depressed Mood) with good model fit (CFI=0.987, TLI=0.985), and the questionnaire demonstrated good reliability (Cronbach's alpha 0.876–0.924 for factors) and convergent validity with other sleep and mood scales.

papers.title: Effect of Thermal Softening of Endotracheal Tubes on Perioperative Respiratory Adverse Events in Children Undergoing Adenotonsillectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 254 children undergoing adenotonsillectomy, pre-warming endotracheal tubes to 37°C significantly reduced the incidence of perioperative respiratory adverse events from 24.6% to 14.1% (p=0.039), with lower rates of laryngospasm (2.3% vs. 8.7%) and postoperative coughing (11.7% vs. 21.4%). Room-temperature tube use and higher Obstructive Sleep Apnea-18 score were independent predictors of such events.

papers.title: Anti‑cancer effects of the circadian clock modulating compound SR9009 in chordoma cell lines.
papers.summary: SR9009, a REV-ERBα agonist, reduced viability of chordoma cell lines in a concentration-dependent manner while sparing normal cells, and inhibited migration and colony formation. Molecular docking predicted high-affinity binding to PI3K, Akt1, Wnt3, β-catenin, and Nanog, suggesting interference with proliferation and survival signaling.

papers.title: A Comparative Randomized Crossover Pilot Study Comparing Male External Urine Collection Devices in Home Settings.
papers.journal: Journal of wound, ostomy, and continence nursing : official publication of The Wound, Ostomy and Continence Nurses Society
papers.summary: In a randomized crossover pilot study of 15 community-dwelling older men requiring nocturnal urine management, a male external catheter with vacuum-assisted collection was compared to a standard condom catheter. The study device showed comparable urine capture rate (98.5% vs. 98.1%) and safety, with strong participant preference for the external collection device (86.7%).

papers.title: Effects of Esketamine on Postoperative Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale Scores in Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Radical Resection for Colorectal Cancer.
papers.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
papers.summary: This randomized placebo-controlled trial investigated intravenous esketamine during laparoscopic radical resection for colorectal cancer. Esketamine significantly reduced postoperative HADS anxiety and depression scores on days 1 and 3, lowered 24-hour interleukin-6 levels, and improved patient satisfaction compared to control.

papers.title: Oronasal blood, intrathoracic petechiae and pulmonary hemorrhages differentiate prone separate-bed from bed-sharing SIDS cases.
papers.summary: In a retrospective review of 313 SIDS cases, bed-sharing SIDS infants had significantly higher mean intra-alveolar hemorrhage scores (3.0 on a 0–4 scale) compared to prone separate-bed SIDS (1.1), while prone separate-bed cases more often exhibited intrathoracic petechiae. The proportion of bed-sharing cases increased from 7% in the 1980s to 52% after 2010, and the findings suggest distinct pathological patterns for bed-sharing versus prone separate-bed SIDS.

papers.title: Awake venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as a bridge to foetal maturation in severe pulmonary hypertension: a case report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 37-year-old pregnant woman with severe pulmonary hypertension who declined termination and was managed with awake venoarterial ECMO as a bridge to fetal maturation. Despite complications requiring intubation and conversion to venoarterial-venous ECMO, urgent caesarean delivery at day 4 resulted in a live birth and both mother and infant survived to discharge.

papers.title: Factors influencing postoperative thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression therapy in low-risk papillary thyroid cancer after lobectomy.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 223 low-risk papillary thyroid cancer patients identified factors associated with TSH suppression outcomes after lobectomy. Excessive TSH suppression was linked to female sex, higher levothyroxine dose, lower preoperative TSH, lower physical activity, and higher sedentary time, while insufficient suppression was associated with higher BMI and lower levothyroxine dose.

papers.title: Burden of Treatment-Induced Vasomotor Symptoms in Men With Prostate Cancer on Androgen-Deprivation Therapy: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.summary: This systematic literature review of 52 studies assessed the burden of treatment-induced vasomotor symptoms (VMS) in men with prostate cancer on androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT). VMS severity, but not frequency, was consistently associated with reduced quality of life, and no validated PRO instrument specific to ADT-induced VMS in prostate cancer was identified.

papers.title: Intraosseous venous malformation of the clivus.
papers.summary: Case report of a teenage female with intermittent right-sided tongue numbness and twitching, diagnosed with an intraosseous venous malformation (cavernous type) of the clivus via biopsy. Empirical propranolol treatment led to symptom resolution and slight lesion size reduction after 2 years, with stability the following year.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
